p0.original: When the division of labour has been once thoroughly established, it is but a very small part of a man's wants which the produce of his own labour can supply. He supplies the far greater part of them by exchanging that surplus part of the produce of his own labour, which is over and above his own consumption, for such parts of the produce of other men's labour as he has occasion for. Every man thus lives by exchanging, or becomes, in some measure, a merchant, and the society itself grows to be what is properly a commercial society.
p0.zh: 当劳动分工一度彻底确定后,他自己的劳动生产所能供应的只是一个人的一小部分愿望. 他通过交换他自己劳动的剩余部分来供应其中的更大部分,这些剩余部分超出了他自己消费的范围,用于他所希望的其他男子劳动的这些部分。 因此,每个人都靠交换生活,或在某种程度上成为商人,而社会本身则发展成为一个适当的商业社会。

p1.original: But when the division of labour first began to take place, this power of exchanging must frequently have been very much clogged and embarrassed in its operations. One man, we shall suppose, has more of a certain commodity than he himself has occasion for, while another has less. The former, consequently, would be glad to dispose of; and the latter to purchase, a part of this superfluity. But if this latter should chance to have nothing that the former stands in need of, no exchange can be made between them. The butcher has more meat in his shop than he himself can consume, and the brewer and the baker would each of them be willing to purchase a part of it. But they have nothing to offer in exchange, except the different productions of their respective trades, and the butcher is already provided with all the bread and beer which he has immediate occasion for. No exchange can, in this case, be made between them. He cannot be their merchant, nor they his customers; and they are all of them thus mutually less serviceable to one another. In order to avoid the inconveniency of such situations, every prudent man in every period of society, after the first establishment of the division of labour, must naturally have endeavoured to manage his affairs in such a manner, as to have at all times by him, besides the peculiar produce of his own industry, a certain quantity of some one commodity or other, such as he imagined few people would be likely to refuse in exchange for the produce of their industry. Many different commodities, it is probable, were successively both thought of and employed for this purpose. In the rude ages of society, cattle are said to have been the common instrument of commerce; and, though they must have been a most inconvenient one, yet, in old times, we find things were frequently valued according to the number of cattle which had been given in exchange for them. The armour of Diomede, says Homer, cost only nine oxen; but that of Glaucus cost a hundred oxen. Salt is said to be the common instrument of commerce and exchanges in Abyssinia; a species of shells in some parts of the coast of India; dried cod at Newfoundland; tobacco in Virginia; sugar in some of our West India colonies; hides or dressed leather in some other countries; and there is at this day a village in Scotland, where it is not uncommon, I am told, for a workman to carry nails instead of money to the baker's shop or the ale-house.
p1.zh: 但是,在第一次开始分工时,这种交换能力在业务中必然经常被堵塞和尴尬。 我们假设一个人拥有的商品比他自己需要的还要多,而另一个人则更少。 因此,前者乐于处置;后者乐于购买这一超级流利的一部分。 但是,如果后者没有机会获得前者需要的东西,它们之间就不能进行交换。屠夫的店里肉量比他自己能消耗的还要多,酿酒师和面包师都愿意购买一部分肉.但他们除了各自行业的不同生产品外,没有任何东西可以交换,屠夫已经得到了他立即需要的所有面包和啤酒. 在这种情况下,他们之间不能进行交换。 他不能做他们的生意,也不能做他们的客人,他们彼此之间互不相干。为了避免这种情况的不便,社会每一时期的每一个谨慎的人,在第一次确立分工之后,都必须自然地努力以这样的方式管理自己的事务,除了他自己行业的奇特产品外,他任何时候都拥有一定数量的某种商品或他所想象的某种商品,如很少有人会拒绝换取其行业的产品. 许多不同的商品,很可能都是为此目的而相继想到和使用的。 在社会粗鲁的年代,据说牛是通商的常用工具;虽然它们一定是最不方便的,但在旧时,我们发现,根据以牛为交换的牛的数量,经常会重视一些东西.狄奥米德的盔甲,荷马说,只花了九头牛;但格劳克斯的盔甲却花了一百头牛. 据说,盐是阿比西尼亚商业和交流的共同工具;印度海岸一些地区的贝壳种类;纽芬兰干鳕鱼;弗吉尼亚烟草;西印度一些殖民地的糖;在另一些国家藏皮或着装皮革;今天苏格兰有一个村庄,我被告知,工人可以携带钉子而不是钱到面包店或啤酒馆。

p2.original: In all countries, however, men seem at last to have been determined by irresistible reasons to give the preference, for this employment, to metals above every other commodity. Metals can not only be kept with as little loss as any other commodity, scarce any thing being less perishable than they are, but they can likewise, without any loss, be divided into any number of parts, as by fusion those parts can easily be re-united again; a quality which no other equally durable commodities possess, and which, more than any other quality, renders them fit to be the instruments of commerce and circulation. The man who wanted to buy salt, for example, and had nothing but cattle to give in exchange for it, must have been obliged to buy salt to the value of a whole ox, or a whole sheep, at a time. He could seldom buy less than this, because what he was to give for it could seldom be divided without loss; and if he had a mind to buy more, he must, for the same reasons, have been obliged to buy double or triple the quantity, the value, to wit, of two or three oxen, or of two or three sheep. If, on the contrary, instead of sheep or oxen, he had metals to give in exchange for it, he could easily proportion the quantity of the metal to the precise quantity of the commodity which he had immediate occasion for.
p2.zh: 然而,在所有国家,男子似乎最终被不可抗拒的理由所决定,要从事这种工作,就应优先考虑金属,而不是其他任何商品。金属不仅可以象其他商品一样少流失,稀有的任何东西都不如它们那么易腐烂,而且它们同样可以不加任何损失地被分成任何一部分,因为通过聚变,这些部件很容易重新组合起来;这种质量没有其他同样耐用商品,而且比任何其他质量更适合成为商业和流通的工具。譬如欲买盐者,只得牛来换取,必有一次买盐,以全牛,或全羊为价. 他很少能买到比这少的钱,因为他要买的东西很少可以分而无损失;而且如果他想买更多的东西,他必须出于同样的原因,不得不买到两倍或三倍的数量,也就是两三头牛或两三头羊的价值。 相反,如果他不是羊或牛,而是有金属作为交换条件,他可以很容易地将金属的数量与他立即需要的商品的确切数量比例。

p3.original: Different metals have been made use of by different nations for this purpose. Iron was the common instrument of commerce among the ancient Spartans, copper among the ancient Romans, and gold and silver among all rich and commercial nations.
p3.zh: 不同国家为此目的使用了不同的金属。铁是古代斯巴达人通商的常用工具,古罗马人通商的铜器,所有富商国家通商的金银器.

p4.original: Those metals seem originally to have been made use of for this purpose in rude bars, without any stamp or coinage. Thus we are told by Pliny (Plin. Hist Nat. lib. 33, cap. 3), upon the authority of Timaeus, an ancient historian, that, till the time of Servius Tullius, the Romans had no coined money, but made use of unstamped bars of copper, to purchase whatever they had occasion for. These rude bars, therefore, performed at this time the function of money.
p4.zh: 这些金属最初似乎被用于无礼的栏杆中,没有任何印章或硬币。 因此,普林尼告诉了我们。夏特纳特 利布 Hist Nat. lib.33,盖.3),在古代历史学家蒂马厄斯的授意下,直到塞尔维乌斯·图利乌斯的时代,罗马人没有硬币,而是利用未加印的铜条,购买他们有的场合. 因此,这些粗鲁的酒吧在这个时候履行了金钱的作用。

p5.original: The use of metals in this rude state was attended with two very considerable inconveniences; first, with the trouble of weighing, and secondly, with that of assaying them. In the precious metals, where a small difference in the quantity makes a great difference in the value, even the business of weighing, with proper exactness, requires at least very accurate weights and scales. The weighing of gold, in particular, is an operation of some nicety in the coarser metals, indeed, where a small error would be of little consequence, less accuracy would, no doubt, be necessary. Yet we should find it excessively troublesome if every time a poor man had occasion either to buy or sell a farthing's worth of goods, he was obliged to weigh the farthing. The operation of assaying is still more difficult, still more tedious; and, unless a part of the metal is fairly melted in the crucible, with proper dissolvents, any conclusion that can be drawn from it is extremely uncertain. Before the institution of coined money, however, unless they went through this tedious and difficult operation, people must always have been liable to the grossest frauds and impositions; and instead of a pound weight of pure silver, or pure copper, might receive, in exchange for their goods, an adulterated composition of the coarsest and cheapest materials, which had, however, in their outward appearance, been made to resemble those metals. To prevent such abuses, to facilitate exchanges, and thereby to encourage all sorts of industry and commerce, it has been found necessary, in all countries that have made any considerable advances towards improvement, to affix a public stamp upon certain quantities of such particular metals, as were in those countries commonly made use of to purchase goods. Hence the origin of coined money, and of those public offices called mints; institutions exactly of the same nature with those of the aulnagers and stamp-masters of woollen and linen cloth. All of them are equally meant to ascertain, by means of a public stamp, the quantity and uniform goodness of those different commodities when brought to market.
p5.zh: 在这种粗鲁状态下使用金属,有两种相当不便;第一,有权衡的麻烦,第二,有检验它们的麻烦. 在贵金属中,如果数量上的微小差异使价值大不相同,即使是量子的作业,只要有适当的精确度,至少需要非常精确的权重和尺度.特别是,金子的重量是较粗金属中某种优美的操作,事实上,在这种操作中,一个小错误不会产生什么后果,毫无疑问,准确性较低是必要的。 然而,我们应该发现这太麻烦了,如果每当一个穷人有机会买到或卖掉远物的商品时,他不得不权衡远物。化验的操作仍然比较困难,仍然比较乏味;并且,除非金属的一部分在熔炉中被相当的熔化,并有适当的溶解物,否则任何从中可以得出的结论都是极其不确定的. 然而,在硬币铸造之前,除非经过这种烦琐而困难的操作,否则人们必定总是会遭受最严重的欺诈和强加行为;而且,人们可能得到一种变质的、最廉价材料的成分,而这种材料在外表上与这些金属类似,而不是纯银或纯铜的磅重。 为了防止这种滥用行为,便利交流,从而鼓励各种工业和商业,在所有在改进方面取得显著进展的国家中,都有必要像那些通常利用这种金属购买货物的国家那样,在某种数量上盖上公章。 因此,硬币来源,以及那些称为薄荷的公职;机构的性质与羊毛布和亚麻布的毛发和印花管理者完全相同。 所有这些商品都同样是为了通过公章确定这些不同商品在进入市场时的数量和统一品质。

p6.original: The first public stamps of this kind that were affixed to the current metals, seem in many cases to have been intended to ascertain, what it was both most difficult and most important to ascertain, the goodness or fineness of the metal, and to have resembled the sterling mark which is at present affixed to plate and bars of silver, or the Spanish mark which is sometimes affixed to ingots of gold, and which, being struck only upon one side of the piece, and not covering the whole surface, ascertains the fineness, but not the weight of the metal. Abraham weighs to Ephron the four hundred shekels of silver which he had agreed to pay for the field of Machpelah. They are said, however, to be the current money of the merchant, and yet are received by weight, and not by tale, in the same manner as ingots of gold and bars of silver are at present. The revenues of the ancient Saxon kings of England are said to have been paid, not in money, but in kind, that is, in victuals and provisions of all sorts. William the Conqueror introduced the custom of paying them in money. This money, however, was for a long time, received at the exchequer, by weight, and not by tale.
p6.zh: 首枚贴在现金属上的这种公共邮票,在许多情况下似乎是为了确定金属的品德和精细程度,以及目前贴在银板和铁条上的精美标记,或者有时贴在金币上的西班牙标记,这些标记只是打在一块石头上,而不是覆盖整个表面,从而确定金属的精细程度,而不是重量。亚伯拉罕向以弗龙重过四百谢克尔的银子,他同意为马奇佩拉赫的田地支付银子. 然而,据说,它们是商人的现货,然而却按重量而不是按故事来接受,就像现在的金币和银条一样。 据说,英格兰古代萨克森诸王的岁月收入已经支付,不是用钱,而是用实物,即用维法和各种供给.征服者威廉引入了以金钱支付他们的习俗. 然而,这笔钱是很长一段时间的,从财政上,从重量上,而不是从故事上,得到的。

p7.original: The inconveniency and difficulty of weighing those metals with exactness, gave occasion to the institution of coins, of which the stamp, covering entirely both sides of the piece, and sometimes the edges too, was supposed to ascertain not only the fineness, but the weight of the metal. Such coins, therefore, were received by tale, as at present, without the trouble of weighing.
p7.zh: 由于不方便和难以精确地权衡这些金属,使硬币的形成成为了一次机会,其中的印章完全覆盖了棋子的两侧,有时也覆盖了边缘,因此应该不仅要确定金属的细微性,还要确定金属的重量. 因此,像目前这样,这种硬币是按故事收到的,没有重担的麻烦。

p8.original: The denominations of those coins seem originally to have expressed the weight or quantity of metal contained in them. In the time of Servius Tullius, who first coined money at Rome, the Roman as or pondo contained a Roman pound of good copper. It was divided, in the same manner as our Troyes pound, into twelve ounces, each of which contained a real ounce of good copper. The English pound sterling, in the time of Edward I. contained a pound, Tower weight, of silver of a known fineness. The Tower pound seems to have been something more than the Roman pound, and something less than the Troyes pound. This last was not introduced into the mint of England till the 18th of Henry the VIII. The French livre contained, in the time of Charlemagne, a pound, Troyes weight, of silver of a known fineness. The fair of Troyes in Champaign was at that time frequented by all the nations of Europe, and the weights and measures of so famous a market were generally known and esteemed. The Scots money pound contained, from the time of Alexander the First to that of Robert Bruce, a pound of silver of the same weight and fineness with the English pound sterling. English, French, and Scots pennies, too, contained all of them originally a real penny-weight of silver, the twentieth part of an ounce, and the two hundred-and-fortieth part of a pound. The shilling, too, seems originally to have been the denomination of a weight. "When wheat is at twelve shillings the quarter," says an ancient statute of Henry III. "then wastel bread of a farthing shall weigh eleven shillings and fourpence". The proportion, however, between the shilling, and either the penny on the one hand, or the pound on the other, seems not to have been so constant and uniform as that between the penny and the pound. During the first race of the kings of France, the French sou or shilling appears upon different occasions to have contained five, twelve, twenty, and forty pennies. Among the ancient Saxons, a shilling appears at one time to have contained only five pennies, and it is not improbable that it may have been as variable among them as among their neighbours, the ancient Franks. From the time of Charlemagne among the French, and from that of William the Conqueror among the English, the proportion between the pound, the shilling, and the penny, seems to have been uniformly the same as at present, though the value of each has been very different; for in every country of the world, I believe, the avarice and injustice of princes and sovereign states, abusing the confidence of their subjects, have by degrees diminished the real quantity of metal, which had been originally contained in their coins. The Roman as, in the latter ages of the republic, was reduced to the twenty-fourth part of its original value, and, instead of weighing a pound, came to weigh only half an ounce. The English pound and penny contain at present about a third only; the Scots pound and penny about a thirty-sixth; and the French pound and penny about a sixty-sixth part of their original value. By means of those operations, the princes and sovereign states which performed them were enabled, in appearance, to pay their debts and fulfil their engagements with a smaller quantity of silver than would otherwise have been requisite. It was indeed in appearance only; for their creditors were really defrauded of a part of what was due to them. All other debtors in the state were allowed the same privilege, and might pay with the same nominal sum of the new and debased coin whatever they had borrowed in the old. Such operations, therefore, have always proved favourable to the debtor, and ruinous to the creditor, and have sometimes produced a greater and more universal revolution in the fortunes of private persons, than could have been occasioned by a very great public calamity.
p8.zh: 这些硬币的面额最初似乎表明了其中所含金属的重量或数量。塞尔维乌斯·图利乌斯最初在罗马铸造钱币时,罗马人作为或庞多含有一磅罗马好铜.和我们的特洛伊斯镑一样,它被分成十二盎司,每一盎司都含有一盎司的真铜.爱德华一世时期的英国英镑 含有一磅 塔的重量 一种已知精美的银子塔币似乎比罗马币还多, 也比特洛伊斯币还少. 这最后一件直到亨利八世的十八世才被引入英格兰的薄荷. 法国的利弗尔在查理曼时代 含有一磅特洛伊斯重量 一种已知精美的银子 当时,所有欧洲国家都经常在香槟的特洛伊斯集市举行,如此著名的市场重量和措施普遍为人所知并备受尊重。 从亚历山大一世到罗伯特·布鲁斯的时代,苏格兰人的钱币中包含着一磅同样重量和精美的银币,与英磅一样.英国、法国和苏格兰的硬币 原本都包含一毛钱的银币 盎司的第二十部分和二百四十磅的 这先令也似乎是重量的面额。"当小麦在12先令的季度," 说一个古老的法规 亨利三世。远物的白蚁面包 将重达11先令和4便士 然而,先令与一分钱或一分钱之间的比例似乎没有像一分钱与一分钱之间的比例那么恒和统一. 在法兰西诸王的首场比赛中,法国的苏或先令在不同场合都出现了5,12,20,40便士的情况. 在古代萨克森人中,一先令一度似乎只包含五便士,而且其中可能和他们的邻居——古法兰克人一样多变,这并非不可能. 从法国人查理曼时代开始,从英国人征服者威廉时代开始,英镑,先令和硬币之间的比例似乎与现在一致,尽管每个币值都有很大不同;因为我认为,在世界上的每一个国家,王子和主权国家的贪婪和不公正,滥用了臣民的信心,在一定程度上减少了原本包含在硬币中的金属的实际数量. 在共和国后期的罗马人被减为原值的第二十四部分,他没有重一磅,反而只重了半盎司.英国镑和一分钱目前只包含约三分之一;苏格兰镑和一分钱大约为三十六;法兰西镑和一分钱大约为原值的六十六部分. 通过这些行动,执行这些行动的王子和主权国家在外表上能够以比其他需要的更少的白银偿还债务和履行承诺。 这确实只是表面上的;因为债权人确实被骗了一部分应得的债务。州内所有其他债务人都享有同样的特权,可能以同样的名义金额支付新币和去基币,无论他们在旧币中借过什么。 因此,这种操作一向对债务人有利,对债权人造成破坏,有时对私人的财富造成比一场非常巨大的公共灾难更大规模的、更普遍的革命。

p9.original: It is in this manner that money has become, in all civilized nations, the universal instrument of commerce, by the intervention of which goods of all kinds are bought and sold, or exchanged for one another.
p9.zh: 正是以这种方式,在所有文明国家中,金钱已经成为世界商业工具,通过干预,各种货物被买卖,或相互交换。

p10.original: What are the rules which men naturally observe, in exchanging them either for money, or for one another, I shall now proceed to examine. These rules determine what may be called the relative or exchangeable value of goods.
p10.zh: 男人自然会遵守什么规则,为了金钱或者为了彼此,我现在将着手研究。这些规则确定货物可称为相对价值或可交换价值。

p11.original: The word VALUE, it is to be observed, has two different meanings, and sometimes expresses the utility of some particular object, and sometimes the power of purchasing other goods which the possession of that object conveys. The one may be called 'value in use;' the other, 'value in exchange.' The things which have the greatest value in use have frequently little or no value in exchange; and, on the contrary, those which have the greatest value in exchange have frequently little or no value in use. Nothing is more useful than water; but it will purchase scarce any thing; scarce any thing can be had in exchange for it. A diamond, on the contrary, has scarce any value in use; but a very great quantity of other goods may frequently be had in exchange for it.
p11.zh: 需要注意的是,VALUE一词有两种不同的含义,有时表达某种特定物体的效用,有时表达购买该物体占有所传递的其他货物的力量.一种可称为“使用价值”;另一种称为“使用价值”。 使用价值最高的事物往往很少或没有价值;相反,使用价值最高的事物往往很少或没有价值。没有什么比水更有用的了;但它会购买稀有的东西;任何稀有的东西都可以用来换取它。 相反,钻石在使用中几乎没有任何价值,但经常会有大量其他货物作为交换。

p12.original: In order to investigate the principles which regulate the exchangeable value of commodities, I shall endeavour to shew,
p12.zh: 为了调查规范商品可交换价值的原则,我将努力使,

p13.original: First, what is the real measure of this exchangeable value; or wherein consists the real price of all commodities.
p13.zh: 首先,这种可交换价值的真正衡量标准是什么;或在所有商品的实际价格中。

p14.original: Secondly, what are the different parts of which this real price is composed or made up.
p14.zh: 第二,这个实际价格构成或构成的不同部分是什么?

p15.original: And, lastly, what are the different circumstances which sometimes raise some or all of these different parts of price above, and sometimes sink them below, their natural or ordinary rate; or, what are the causes which sometimes hinder the market price, that is, the actual price of commodities, from coinciding exactly with what may be called their natural price.
p15.zh: 最后,有时将价格的某些或所有不同部分抬高,有时将价格降低到自然或普通价格以下,或者,有时阻碍市场价格,即初级商品的实际价格的原因是什么,与所谓的自然价格完全一致。

p16.original: I shall endeavour to explain, as fully and distinctly as I can, those three subjects in the three following chapters, for which I must very earnestly entreat both the patience and attention of the reader: his patience, in order to examine a detail which may, perhaps, in some places, appear unnecessarily tedious; and his attention, in order to understand what may perhaps, after the fullest explication which I am capable of giving it, appear still in some degree obscure. I am always willing to run some hazard of being tedious, in order to be sure that I am perspicuous; and, after taking the utmost pains that I can to be perspicuous, some obscurity may still appear to remain upon a subject, in its own nature extremely abstracted.
p16.zh: 我将努力尽可能充分、明确地解释以下三个章节中的这三个主题,对此我必须恳求读者的耐心和注意:他的耐心,以便研究一个细节,也许在某些地方,这种细节可能显得不必要地乏味;他的注意,以便理解,在最充分解释之后,我可能能够给予它的东西,在某种程度上似乎仍然模糊不清。 我总是愿意冒一些烦躁的危险,以便确定我是否敏锐;而且,在承受我所能敏锐的极大痛苦之后,有些模糊似乎仍然停留在一个主题上,从其本身的性质来看,它极其抽象。
